articles.title: Kosatka 0.2: what is new
articles.body:
A new version of the engine is out. The highlights: template safety, shared script mechanisms and a new theme.

In short

  • Text is output as HTML only for fields with a text format.
  • Logging out is a POST request.
  • Confirmations, drag and drop and autocomplete share one piece of code driven by data attributes.

To update, run app migrate -apply after deploying.

comments.author: ishmael
comments.body: Finally! Updated in five minutes, everything works.

replies.author: starbuck
replies.body: Glad to hear it. If anything comes up, write here.

comments.author: queequeg
comments.body: Will there be a dark theme?

replies.author: starbuck
replies.body: Already there: the switch in the header.

articles.title: Meet Kosatka CMS
articles.body:
Kosatka is a content management system written in Go. Content types, fields, lists and menus are set up in the admin, without touching the code.

What the engine does

  • Content types with their own fields: text, dates, images, files, links, terms.
  • Lists (Views) with filters, sorting and paging.
  • Blocks and regions, menus, breadcrumbs, SEO patterns.
  • Modules: galleries, polls, forms, feeds, ratings.

A site runs on MySQL or PostgreSQL and ships as a single binary.

comments.author: jim_hawkins
comments.body: A good overview for a first look.

articles.title: How themes work
articles.body:
A theme changes the look without touching the data. It can override any template of the engine or only a part of one - say, how the fields are shown on a content page.

A good theme overrides the layout, not the engine's logic.

Without a theme a site is shown in the engine's neutral look - the one you see now. It is light or dark, following your system's setting.

comments.author: ishmael
comments.body: I overrode just the card and took the rest from the engine. Handy.

replies.author: captain_nemo
replies.body: That is the idea: a theme doesn't copy the engine.

articles.title: Lists and feeds without programming
articles.body:
The feed on the front page is an ordinary View: it has its fields, filters and sorting. Change it in the admin, or add other lists - by section, by tag, by author.

Display styles

A list, a grid, a table or a carousel. Every field has its own format: an image style, a date format, a text length.

comments.author: queequeg
comments.body: Views take a couple of minutes to build, with no code at all.

replies.author: starbuck
replies.body: Yes: by year, month or day.

articles.title: Modules are switched on in the admin
articles.body:
Galleries, polls and forms are modules. They are switched on and off on the Modules page; a module switched off keeps its data, and an uninstalled one removes it along with its tables.

Every module brings its own routes, pages and status checks. A module can also live in a repository of its own, like the forum: the site adds it to its binary.

articles.title: The status report
articles.body:
The Reports section has the status report: the engine's version, the database, the modules and the checks - pending database updates, file directories, mail, the site's address.

When something is wrong, the admin shows a warning at the top of every page. Database updates are applied with one command:

./kosatka migrate -apply

articles.title: Running in Docker
articles.body:
All it takes to try the engine is Docker:

docker compose up --build

The site opens at localhost:8080, and the administrator's password is in the container's log: docker compose logs app.

comments.author: captain_nemo
comments.body: The Docker image started on the first try.

comments.author: long_john_silver
comments.body: A fine thing, this Docker: up went the site and not a soul the wiser. Pieces of eight!

articles.title: Tags and sections
articles.body:
Taxonomy vocabularies describe content: one section per article, as many tags as you like. Every term has its own page listing its content.

How it works

A vocabulary is created in the admin, a term field is added to a content type. The field widget is a select list, radio buttons, checkboxes or autocomplete.

Terms are data: rename them without touching templates.

comments.author: ishmael
comments.body: Tags with autocomplete are just what I needed.

articles.title: Comments and moderation
articles.body:
Comments are threaded: any of them can be replied to. The comment mode is set for a content type and for each item - open, closed or hidden.

Moderation

New content from users with the "on moderation" permission waits for review. The waiting list is in the admin bar, and every item shows its status.

articles.title: A forum from its own repository
articles.body:
The Forum module lives in a repository of its own: a site adds it to its binary with app module add and enables it on the Modules page. It is built on a vocabulary: root terms are categories, child terms are sections with topics. Topics are ordinary content, replies are comments.

  • Sticky and hot topics.
  • Active topics and topics without replies.
  • Members' signatures and avatars.

comments.author: jim_hawkins
comments.body: We moved our old forum: topics and replies are all there.

replies.author: queequeg
replies.body: Did the signatures come over too?

articles.title: Polls and forms
articles.body:
A poll is a content type with answer options: voting without reloading the page, results as bars. Forms collect submissions: fields, required ones, visibility conditions, email notifications.

Both modules are switched on on the Modules page and off the same way.

articles.title: SEO without plugins
articles.body:
The page title and meta description are built from templates with tokens: for a content type, for a rule with a condition, for a vocabulary. Every item can set its own.

What else

  • A sitemap and robots.txt.
  • Canonical URLs and redirects from old addresses.
  • Breadcrumbs by rules.

comments.author: queequeg
comments.body: Templates with tokens save a lot of time.

articles.title: Site search
articles.body: Live search suggests content as you type, and the results page shows everything found, page by page. Which types are searched and in what order is set in the admin.

articles.title: Permissions and roles
articles.body:
Permissions are given to roles, roles to users. Modules declare their own permissions, and they show up in the shared matrix.

The "User" role holds the permissions of anyone logged in.

Required profile fields are asked for at registration and after logging in with a social network.

articles.title: Faster with caching
articles.body:
Pages for guests are cached, View blocks are rebuilt in the background, images are served in styles of the right size. The cache lifetime is set on the Performance page.

For a CDN the engine sends caching headers, and a guest's form or login doesn't break the cache: the page's script fetches the CSRF token separately.

page.title: About
page.body:
This site runs on Kosatka, a content management system written in Go.

The articles on the front page and this page are demo content, added at installation. Edit or delete them in the admin, on the Content page, and add your own.
